summary: The HUD loads at desktop and mobile sizes, but the application fails at runtime: node_modules/cannon-es/dist/cannon-es.js returns HTTP 404 on every load, no canvas is created, and all course, physics, camera, and result functionality is unavailable.

runtime.reason: The page shell renders, but the critical cannon-es module request returns 404 on initial load and after reload. A read-only DOM probe found zero canvas elements; Release, Space, Retry, and Reset all leave the attempt count at 00 and the course area blank.

scene.reason: No 3D scene or canvas exists because initialization fails before a renderer is created, so geometry, depth, occlusion, materials, lighting, and camera behavior cannot be inspected.

checks.reason: The viewport contains no canvas or rendered course, so task-relevant depth and geometry cannot be inspected from any view.

The surrounding HUD is clean and legible at both viewport sizes, and its typography/color hierarchy is coherent, but the course composition, materials, and lighting requested by the task are entirely absent.
The primary Release button and the advertised Space shortcut produce no scene change, no status change, and no attempt-count increment.
Retry and Reset all are clickable but cause no observable state change, and Pause is disabled; no repeat or recovery flow can execute because there is no active simulation.

Both 1440x900 and 390x844 layouts render the HUD without horizontal overflow, mobile lower controls remain visible, and keyboard focus is visible; however, reload repeats the missing cannon-es 404 and the primary 3D experience never loads. Console and network details are recorded in evidence/console.txt and evidence/network.txt.
No tabletop course is rendered, so elevated ramps, guardrails, the jump gap, and the marked finish basin are all absent.
With no canvas or running simulation, neither Release nor Space produces a marble, gravity response, fall, bounce, or visible collision.
The launch-impulse range thumb can be moved natively to its end, but the displayed value remains 62%, no ramp geometry exists to move, and no trajectory or collision outcome changes.
No attempt can be started and no success is detected; the attempt counter remains 00, so no settings combination can reach the absent finish basin.
Release does not start an attempt, setup controls remain visually available rather than locking, the counter stays at 00, and no off-course failure can occur or be reported.
Pause is disabled, Retry and Reset all produce no visible result, and there is no active marble motion or settings/count state to preserve or restore.

Course and Follow buttons are present, but there is no rendered course or marble camera to inspect or follow; orbit and zoom therefore have no 3D effect. The mobile layout is visible, but real touch hardware was not available to verify.

instruction.reason: Not scored because the page fails to run, preventing evaluation of the requested playable flow; the rubric directs null quality scores for runtime failure.

spatial.reason: Not scored because no 3D scene or canvas is created, so spatial quality cannot be evaluated.

interaction.reason: Not scored because the application runtime fails before interactions can affect a scene or simulation state.

visual.reason: Not scored because the 3D visual subject never renders, although the surrounding HUD is visible.

stability.reason: Not scored because the page has a reproducible core resource failure on initial load and reload.

limitations: No 3D scene, canvas, or camera existed, so depth, materials, lighting, occlusion, physics quality, success behavior, and camera-follow smoothness could not be evaluated.
Mobile testing used a 390x844 viewport, but real touch hardware was unavailable; touch-specific behavior remains unverified.
No download or export action was advertised or available to inspect.
Browser-only observation cannot establish the intended physics-library implementation; the network log does identify a missing cannon-es module.
